chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Hasan ibn Mu'awiya, from Muhammad ibn Hammad (the brother of Yusuf ibn Hammad al-Khazzaz), from al-'Aziz al-Qaratisi, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and mentioned to him some matters of the Shias and their sayings. He said: 'O Aziz, Faith has ten ranks, like a ladder that has ten rungs, and one ascends from it rung after rung. So the owner of the first rank should not say to the owner of the second,
You are not upon anything (i.e., you have no faith).
And the owner of the second should not say to the owner of the third, 'You are not upon anything,' until it reaches the tenth rank.
He said: Salman was in the tenth, Abu Dharr in the ninth, and Miqdad in the eighth.

O Aziz, do not dismiss those who are below you, lest those above you dismiss you. When you see one who is below you, if you are able to raise him to your rank gently, then do so. And do not burden him with what he cannot bear, lest you break him. For whoever breaks a believer, he must mend him, because if you try to carry a young camel with the load of an adult camel, you will break its back.
ai.seo_question: What are the ten ranks of faith and how should believers treat those with lower ranks?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to illustrate the hierarchical yet interconnected nature of Iman, emphasizing that spiritual status is relative and dynamic rather than static. The Imam uses the examples of Salman al-Farsi, Abu Dharr, and Miqdad to demonstrate that even the most revered companions occupy specific ranks, urging the community to maintain humility and avoid spiritual arrogance. This teaching underscores the practical ethic of 'tadarruj' (gradual progression), where the knowledgeable must gently elevate others without causing them to collapse under the weight of expectations.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-50 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan (ra) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Al-Hassan ibn Muawiyah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hammad - the brother of Yusuf ibn Himad al-Khazzaz, on the authority of Abdul Aziz al-Qaratisi, “I went to see Aba Abdillah (as) and told him about some of the issues of the Shias, and what they say.

He (the Imam) said, ‘O Abdul Aziz! Belief has ten ranks, just like a ladder that has ten steps. One must climb it step by step.
One who has attained two of these ranks should not say to the one who has only attained the first rank, ‘You are not upon anything (You do not have faith).’
One who has attained three of these ranks should not say to the one who has only attained the first two ranks, ‘You are not upon anything.’
The same thing holds true up until the tenth rank.‘ He (the Imam) then said, ‘Salman was in the tenth (rank), Abu Dharr was in the ninth and Miqdad was in the eighth.

O Abdul Aziz! You should not consider anyone who has attained a rank lower than yourself to lack faith, so that those who have attained a higher rank than you have do not consider you to lack faith. When you see someone who is in a lower rank than you are, kindly assist him up to your rank, and do not force upon him what he cannot tolerate, since you may break him (hurt him) this way. One who breaks (hurts) a believer should help him get unhurt; because if you place the load that you would normally place on a nine-year old camel on a baby camel, you would break its back (and kill it).’”
